subject: oop
question: Should a class be declared abstract if it does not define every method inherited from an interface?
title: Unfinished Means Abstract
hook: Builder finished three rooms out of five. Is the house done?
answer: Yes. A class that does not implement all the methods of an interface must be declared abstract.
Otherwise the compiler reports an error.
An abstract class cannot be instantiated.
A concrete subclass must implement the missing methods.
